name.text: Volumes of Solids of Revolution-Washer method-q3

questiontext.text:
Find the volume of the solid generated by revolving the region bounded by \(y={@y1@}\) and \(y={@y2@}\) on the interval \( \displaystyle \left[0,{@interval_2@} \displaystyle \right ]\) about \(x-axis\) using the disk Washer method.

The figure formed when revolved is as shown below

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Since the revolution is about the \(x-axis\), we can use the disk washer method to find the volume as follows.

\( \begin{align} V&=\displaystyle \int_{a}^{b}\pi([f(x)]^2-[g(x)]^2)dx\\ &=\displaystyle \int_{0}^{{@interval_2@}}\pi([{@y2@}]^2-[{@y1@}]^2)dx\\ &=\displaystyle \int_{0}^{{@interval_2@}}\pi([1-\sin^2(\frac{x}{2})]-[\sin^2(\frac{x}{2})])dx\\ &=\displaystyle \int_{0}^{{@interval_2@}}\pi([1-2\sin^2(\frac{x}{2})])dx\\ &=\displaystyle \int_{0}^{{@interval_2@}}\pi \cos(x)dx\\ \end{align} \)

use the trigonometric identity

\(\displaystyle \int \cos (x)\,dx=sin(x)+C\)

Applying the integral we have,

\(\begin{align} \displaystyle \int_{0}^{{@interval_2@}}\pi \cos(x)dx &=\pi \displaystyle \left[ \sin(x) \displaystyle \right ]_0^{{@interval_2@}} \\ &=\pi \displaystyle \left[ \sin({@interval_2@})-\sin(0) \displaystyle \right]\\ \end{align}\)

Since \(\displaystyle \sin⁡ {@interval_2@}=\displaystyle {@sol3@}\) and \(\sin(0)=0\) we have,

\( \pi \cdot ({@sol3@}-0)=\displaystyle{@ta@}\)

Therefore the volume of the solid is \(\displaystyle{@ta@}\)
